checks.comparison: deadline_updates: if deadline (V/4) R j < top then arrivals exist for all k < jR and ofReal(clock after jR updates) <= deadline j, i.e. the first jR updates are performed by T_j (L1428-1435). True by induction with window_updates (T0 := clock of update jR <= T_j, roundTime_mono).
roundTime_mono: for V_i monotone on [0,inf), 0 <= s <= s': roundTime V S s <= roundTime V S s' (the feasible set for s' is contained in that for s since V_i s <= V_i s'). True; exactly the clause.

advance_ringmaster: for any oracle answer ans k (some (pts, sts)) b = Option.elim (event k sts) none (r => some (r.1, r.2, g (pts r.1) b)) (an arrival rule driven by start times, gradient at the arriving worker's point with the k-th sample), if the rule produces arrivals for all k < K, then after k <= K calls the ringmaster state is: count k, point x^k of delayedIterate with masked delays a'_m = delays m (m < K) else m, points i = x^{iters i}, starts/iters/clock of timing, chosen j, selected = x^j if j <= k else x0. delays_bound: a'_k <= k < a'_k + R (L1371). timing_invariant/count/some describe the schedule; advance_add composes runs. I traced step/timingStep: true.

Finiteness of T(R,T_0) is replaced by any T >= 0 with R <= sum_i floor(V_i T/4 - V_i T_0/4); with V_i = work(v_i) this is exactly a feasible point of the set defining T(R,T_0) (L900), so taking T = the attained minimum gives the source statement. A generalization, not a strengthening.
window_updates starts from step m with T_0 = (timing R (completionEvent V) m).clock, the time of update m (when iteration m starts; 0 for m = 0), given that the first m arrivals exist (hm).

Conclusion: arrivals exist for all k < m + R and the clock after update m+R is <= T, i.e. updates m..m+R-1 are performed by T (L898). I checked it is true: within the window each worker is stopped at most once (after a restart at update u >= m+1 its delay stays < R up to update m+R), so worker i completes at least max(floor(w_i) - 1, 0) gradients in [T_0, T] with w_i = V_i(T) - V_i(T_0), and sum_i max(floor(w_i)-1,0) >= sum_i floor(w_i/4) >= R as in L1088-1094; T < T_0 is impossible because then all floors are <= 0 < R. completion_clock gives the ordering invariants (starts <= clock <= pending completions); floor_quarter_le is the arithmetic step.

Conclusions are conjunctions (existence of arrivals and clock bound); hypotheses are the window condition or finiteness of the deadline; correct polarity.
Only continuity and monotonicity of V on [0,inf) are assumed (consequences of PowerAssumption for work v_i via RennalaUniform.work_properties); no extra condition.
floor(V_i T/4 - V_i T0/4) = floor(1/4 int_{T0}^T v_i); floor_quarter_le: w < (2+c)/4 -> floor w <= c (true since (2+c)/4 <= c+1).
Statements track exactly ringmaster's step and the stop rule (iters <= count < iters + R).
advance_ringmaster is pathwise in the sample sequence w, with call c using w c: the k-th applied gradient uses the k-th sample (accepted A3 interpretation).

Together with stoch's iteration_accuracy these give T51: deadline_updates supplies the K arrivals and the clock bound, advance_ringmaster the execution, delays_bound the window hypothesis.
j = 0 / Kbar = 0: deadline 0 = 0 and clock 0; no-arrival events leave timing unchanged; masked delays beyond K satisfy the window; R = 1 gives no delay.
